scope: Disposable PostgreSQL SQL-only diagnosis on one synthetic inventory; no HTTP concurrency, browser, production configuration or release qualification

environment.inventory: 10000 synthetic published Listings with Bulgarian and rotating approved translations

method.settings: SET LOCAL jit on/off inside the same transaction and verified with SHOW jit
method.sequence: For each stage, warm JIT on and off, then measure on/off/off/on against the same analyzed inventory; compare baseline, candidate index, and baseline after dropping the index
method.candidateIndex: current_publications (locale, destination, state, listing_id) INCLUDE (manifest_id, generation, activated_at)

interpretation: JIT compilation explains roughly 500 ms of this standalone eligibility count EXPLAIN at 10000 rows; its reported scan-node time overlaps that compilation time and is not an additive scan cost.

The same transaction-scoped JIT setting did not materially change the end-to-end searchListings call in these paired SQL probes, so the count-query result does not justify a global JIT setting change for the failed HTTP load.

The candidate current_publications index was not selected in any stage; with JIT off, the existing sequential scan itself read 10000 rows in about 1.2 to 1.5 ms from shared hits. Do not add this index as a performance fix.
All five budgeted p95 lanes in the separate two-replica HTTP load remain failed. A causal runtime correction and same-candidate HTTP rerun are still required.
